title: Cue anchoring mini-library — scratchpad
body:
Purpose:
Quick personal library of small, composable cue-anchoring templates and few-shot kits I can copy-paste into tests. Not a polished canonical set — intentionally terse, with failure notes and TODOs.

Context / why this exists:
- Trying to reduce instruction drift when different applications reuse the same base instruction.
- Need compact anchor cues that are token-cheap and robust across temperature/bandwidth variations.
- Want to capture common brittle cases we see in playground tests (role bleed, hallucinated constraints, shot-order sensitivity).

Quick rules-of-thumb I want to remember:
- Anchor phrase near top + short role declaration reduces role bleed more than longer narrative examples.
- A single clear example that demonstrates error-free output beats three fuzzy examples for constrained formats.
- Put explicit "Do not" lines for common hallucination triggers (dates, invented citations).
- If the task is multi-step, split anchor into "goal -> constraints -> example" rather than mixing.

Anchor templates (copyable):
1) Minimal role-anchor (low tokens)
---
You are an accuracy-focused assistant.
Respond in JSON with keys: {"answer": string}.
Example:
Q: "List 2 scientific reasons a bike helmet reduces head injury."
A: {"answer": "1) ...\n2) ..."}
---
Notes: Use for short payloads; good when we care about strict schema.

2) Constraint-first anchor (for safety/format)
---
Goal: produce a single-sentence summary.
Constraints: max 28 words; avoid speculative language; no dates.
Example:
Input: "Paper: multimodal retrieval"
Output: "A retrieval model that fuses image and text features to improve recall."
---
Notes: Helps stop creative elaboration.

3) Few-shot scaffold for instruction-following (3-shot compact)
---
Instruction: Convert notes to bullets, maintain original meaning.
Example 1: "Had trouble with wheels" -> "- Difficulty with wheel assembly"
Example 2: "Remember to pack charger" -> "- Pack charger"
Example 3: "Call before 3pm or send voicemail" -> "- Call before 3pm; leave voicemail if no answer"
Now convert: {{input_text}}
---
Notes: Put a clear delim after examples to anchor expectations. Shot order matters: examples from simple->complex.

Failure cases observed (field notes):
- Role bleed when the phrase "You are" appears mid-prompt: model resets role context. Move "You are" to very top.
- Hallucinated constraints: when examples use parentheses with meta-comments, model sometimes treats them as new constraints. Avoid parentheticals in examples.
- Format decay over long chains: after long convo, the model drops JSON keys. Consider repeating schema anchor as final line before response.

Adversarial few-shots to expose brittleness (for tests):
- Swap expected order in one example (example shows name,last) but label says first,last -> causes ordering errors.
- Introduce an example that intentionally includes a subtle edge-case (empty field, ambiguous pronoun) to check robustness.
- Include one contradictory example (good for probing whether model copies examples verbatim).

Mini test plan (for local harness):
- 1) Stability sweep: temp=0.0,0.2,0.7; top_p 0.9; test 20 varied inputs per anchor template. Log schema violations.
- 2) Shot-order test: permute examples within few-shot scaffold to measure sensitivity.
- 3) Prefix vs suffix anchor: place the same anchor at start and at end of prompt to see where the model honors it more.

Metrics to track (quick):
- schema_violation_rate (percent of responses not matching expected format)
- hallucination_flag_count (subjective human labels; aim < 3%)
- token_overhead (median extra tokens from anchor)

Note-to-self: Add automated parser that tags schema violations for JSON/CSV outputs. Can reuse small harness from GH PR #217.

Examples (few-shot bank) — copy for experiments:
- Task: extract product attributes into YAML-like bullets
Shots:
1) "Blue, size M, cotton tee, limited edition" -> "- color: blue\n- size: M\n- material: cotton\n- edition: limited"
2) "Black running shoes; size 10 (men); waterproof" -> "- color: black\n- category: running shoes\n- size: 10\n- features: waterproof"
Test input: "Red hoodie, L, fleece, washed finish"

- Task: convert informal bug note to triage card
Shot:
1) "Buttons disappear on iOS after lock" -> "Title: Buttons missing on iOS lock\nSeverity: P2\nSteps: ..."
Test input: "App crashes when toggling wifi during upload"

Prompt engineering quick wins observed:
- Repeating the schema right before the input reduces trailing commentary (e.g., add: "Return only the YAML list; no commentary.").
- Explicit token budget instruction sometimes causes the model to truncate helpful context; prefer word/line limits instead.

Open TODOs:
- Convert this scratchpad into a small canonical "mini-kit" directory under GH with runnable tests.
- Try anchors with explicit "anchor-id" that we can reference from RLHF eval logs to correlate failure types.
- Validate on dedicated infra (INF-4821) to confirm latency doesn't change behavior.
- Share with Ethan for his failure-case corpus and integrate top 5 adversarial examples.

Quick unresolved questions:
- Do we prefer role-anchor or constraint-first anchors by default in Redwood hosted API docs? (prod docs currently use role-anchor; might be worth a small A/B).
- How often do anchors increase token billing materially? need a small billing simulation.

Notes to self (random):
- When copying examples into GH, strip long parenthetical notes.
- Keep one-line anchors under ~18 tokens for mobile clients.

Experiment log (headlines):
- 2025-11-10: Initial tests show schema_violation_rate 23% without final schema repeat; drops to 6% when schema repeated immediately before user input.
- 2026-01-12: Observed role bleed in mult-turn session after function call -> need tighter anchor reassertion after a tool call.

End.
